gap: No result ChatGPT got states talk time (hours on calls per charge). The figures they do give are music-playback ratings, and on calls the ranking flips: the Jabra Evolve3 85 is rated for 21 h of talk with ANC on (2.6 eight-hour call days) against 55 h of music, while the Sony WH-1000XM6 is rated for 24 h of talk with NC on (3.0 call days).
standout_why: I opened SoundGuys' 'best noise canceling headphones for work' page (cited in both chats). It gives only music or general battery hours: Jabra Evolve3 85 '55 hr with ANC on', Sony WH-1000XM6 '30 hr' rated and 37 h 14 min in its own test, Sennheiser and Logitech overall hours. It states no talk time for any pick, so a reader would conclude the Jabra lasts almost twice as long as the Sony on calls. The opposite is true. I also opened RTINGS' 'Best Bluetooth Headsets For Phone Calls' (cited in chat 1) and What Hi-Fi's 'Best headphones with a mic' (cited in chat 2), but both returned only page navigation, not article text, so I could not confirm what they say about talk time. ChatGPT's answers give no battery figure except the Sennheiser Momentum 4's '60 hours', which is also a playback number.
decides: This confirms the Sony WH-1000XM6 as the all-rounder pick for someone who is on calls all day: it has more rated call hours with noise cancelling on (24 h vs 21 h) and costs less ($379.99 at Target vs the $486.89 ChatGPT showed for the Jabra). The Jabra's case has to rest on its mic and office features, not battery life. Among the products Dealectric lists, the soundcore Space 2 Pro is the value call headset at about $10 per rated talk hour vs about $15.83 for the Sony.
